items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: When she left, we got a woman named Miss Fields

ctx.x: Of course, she was English, anyway.

Yeah. Well it was cheaper. You see, when Arthur Lyons came home, he sold his rights for $40,000. And he came home, and the show lost its standard. Because it was now, these Europeans were -- Goldberg taught them, taught Leonidow and Seroda, was a Polish pianist that had taken over, had been a concert pianist, and he had some money. And Goldberg, a cheap, an American Jewish man. He taught them how to get things cheaper. And by doing that, he lost the standard of a first class production that had opened up. And if…
